rationale: The target, hazard, SG-1 and FR-7 establish whether required braking occurs or is omitted as the phenomenon to characterise. Braking response is therefore legitimately included. However, the declared scope also incorporates obstacle detection and distance-information production. The requirements and architecture establish these as supporting perception functions, but their influence on braking does not establish them as constituents of the phenomenon being evaluated.
determining_elements: “Braking-maneuver decision and execution state” has a supported core insofar as it characterises whether required braking is produced or omitted.
The explicit inclusion of “obstacle detection” extends P into an observation function described by FR-7.2 and implemented by Object Detection.

“Distance-to-obstacle information,” insofar as it includes the information determined by Sensor Fusion under FR-7.2.4, incorporates a supporting perception output rather than merely the physical vehicle–obstacle relationship relevant to requiring braking.
The qualifier “relevant to whether braking is omitted” establishes relevance, but does not justify including the supporting perception functions within P.
